repair.public_sizes_and_indices: Exact unbounded public integers, including fft_l permutation indices; free construction arithmetic.
repair.threshold_constant: In every recomposition iteration encode the complete public integer i+1 into T[2*l ... nprime-1], zero padded; T[nprime]=0. This replaces the single-limb T[2*l]=i+1 store.
repair.carry_accumulator: Use exact signed two-complement width w_cc=2*k+128, implemented as64-bit chunks, solely for recomposition cc; native limb data and kernelADD/ADC remain64-bit.
repair.final_sign: Compare signed cc to integer-1,0,1 exactly. On the normalized source domain the completed-prefix invariant proves cc is-1or0. Convert carry results returned by add_1 to exact0or1.

capacity_proof.conclusion: 64*(nprime-2*l)>k+2; every i+1<=2^k fits its full k+1bits below limb nprime.

carry_proof.elementary_increment_range: Each reconstruction iteration changes cc by one carry minus two borrows, each0or1; conservative|cc|<=2K+2 at all elementary updates.
carry_proof.invariant: X=R+cc*B^pla,0<=R<B^pla; hence cc in{-1,0} after each complete iteration.
carry_proof.retained_positive_carry_loop: If defensive cc=1branch is retained, the add_1carry loop executes at most twice: a carry1clears its entire target, then a second add1cannotcarry.

additional_gate_charge.wide_cc_updates: At most3K signed-bit updates on w_cc bits; explicit ripple add/sub-by-one-bit uses <=2w_cc AND and<=4w_cc XOR per update.
additional_gate_charge.comparison: Three constant equalities: each<=w_cc AND and<=3w_cc XOR.
additional_gate_charge.public_constant: Fixed bit constants and routing are free inxag-straightline-v1; any separately counted store/clear instructions remain in the source upper census.
additional_gate_charge.coarse_for_p_ge400: k<=p, w_cc<=3p: additional updates+comparisons <=18Kp+9p AND and<=36Kp+27p XOR, absorbed only when the full upper ledger explicitly includes them.

scope: Local semantic extension and gate charge. Does not close the global source-helper loop census, formal verification, full GMP upper or physical execution.
